task: Connect the two blue Cat5e cables from the old phone block to new keystone jacks, join them with a patch cord, then test the link
job_title: Terminate two Cat5e cables to keystones
tools_needed: Punch-down tool (a small handle with a blade tip that presses wire into a keystone jack slot and trims the excess)
110-blade keystone jacks, qty 2 (the small snap-in sockets the patch cord will plug into)
Short patch cord (a pre-made network cable with RJ-45 plugs on both ends)
Cable tester (a two-piece device that sends a signal through all 8 wires and lights up to show pass/fail)
Keystone coupler or surface-mount box to hold the two finished jacks (optional but strongly recommended)

step.title: Photograph the existing punch-down wiring
step.action: Before touching anything, take a clear close-up photo of every wire already seated in the old phone block (the tan or white plastic block with colored wires pressed into numbered slots). This is your undo map if anything goes wrong.
do_not_touch: black thick power or alarm cables
any RJ-45 patch ports already in use on the panel
step.stop_condition: If any wire or terminal looks scorched, melted, or smells burnt, stop and contact a licensed electrician.
step.evidence_required: A photo showing all wire colors and their slot positions on the old punch-down block, sharp enough to read the color labels.
